1.q: The word of Yahweh came to me again
1.note: The phrase “the word of Yahweh came” is an idiom that is used to introduce something that God told his prophets or his people. Alternate translation: [Yahweh spoke to me again]

2.q: What do you mean, you who use this proverb & ‘Fathers eat sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are made blunt’?
2.note: Yahweh asks this rhetorical question to remind Ezekiel something he already knows. The question is a rebuke for the people who use the proverb. Alternate translation: [The people in the land of Israel have this proverb … ‘Fathers eat sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are made blunt’.]

2.q: What do you mean, you who use this proverb
2.note: Here the word “you” is plural and refers to the people of Israel.
This refers to the people of Israel.

2.q: Fathers eat sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are made blunt
2.note: This proverbs means that children experience the consequences of their parents’ actions.

2.q: the children’s teeth are made blunt
2.note: The idiom “teeth are made blunt” refers to the sour taste in one’s mouth that is a result of eating unripe or sour fruit. Alternate translation: [the children get a sour taste in their mouths]

4.note: The word “Behold” here alerts us to pay attention to the surprising information that follows.
Here the word “soul” represents the person. Alternate translation: [The person who sins]

6.q: he does not eat upon the mountains
6.note: People often worshiped and offered sacrifices to pagan gods on the mountains. It is implied that this person has not participated in these kinds of pagan rituals. Alternate translation: [he does not eat meat sacrificed to idols on the mountains]

6.q: lift up his eyes to the idols
6.note: The idiom “lift up his eyes” refers to looking toward something. With reference to idols, this gesture represents worshiping or praying to idols. Alternate translation: [worship the idols] or [pray to the idols]

The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelite people group]

6.q: approached a woman during her monthly period
6.note: It is implicit that he has not approached a woman in order to sleep with her. Alternate translation: [approached a woman to sleep with her during her monthly period]

7.q: gives back to the debtor what was put up as security for a loan
7.note: Alternate translation: [returns to the debtor the item that the debtor gave him as security for the loan]

8.note: This word refers to the money paid by a person to use borrowed money. However, some modern versions interpret “any interest” in this passage as “too much interest.”
This means that he judges fairly the disputes that may arise between people.

9.q: that man walks in my statutes
9.note: Yahweh speaks of a person obeying his statutes as if the statutes were a path in which the person walks. Alternate translation: [that man obeys my statutes]

10.note: This phrase represents murder in any form. Alternate translation: [who murders]
This refers to the sinful actions that Yahweh had mentioned beginning in Ezekiel 18:5.

11.note: People often worshiped and offered sacrifices to pagan gods on the mountains. It is implied that this person has participated in these kinds of pagan rituals. See how you translated a similar phrase in Ezekiel 18:5. Alternate translation: [eats meat sacrificed to idols upon the mountains]

12.note: The words “poor” and “needy” share similar meanings and emphasize that these are people who cannot help themselves.

12.q: he lifts up his eyes to the idols
12.note: The idiom “lifts up his eyes” refers to looking toward something. With reference to idols, this gesture represents worshiping or praying to idols. See how you translated a similar phrase in Ezekiel 18:6. Alternate translation: [he worships the idols] or [he prays to the idols]

13.note: This word refers to the money paid by a person to use borrowed money. However, some modern versions interpret “any interest” in this passage as “too much interest.”

13.q: should that man live? Surely he will not!
13.note: Yahweh asks this as a leading question in order to emphasize the negative answer. Alternate translation: [he will certainly not live!]

13.q: his blood will be on him
13.note: Here the word “blood” represents death. For blood to be on a person is an idiom that means the person is responsible for that death. Alternate translation: [he will be responsible for his own death] (See also: [Idiom](ta:figs-idiom))

14.note: The word “behold” here adds emphasis to what follows.

15.q: That son does not eat upon the mountains
15.note: People often worshiped and offered sacrifices to pagan gods on the mountains. It is implied that this person has not participated in these kinds of pagan rituals. See how you translated a similar phrase in Ezekiel 18:6. Alternate translation: [That son does not eat meat sacrificed to idols upon the mountains]

15.q: he does not lift up his eyes to the idols
15.note: The idiom “lifted up his eyes” refers to looking toward something. With reference to idols, this gesture represents worshiping or praying to idols. See how you translated a similar phrase in Ezekiel 18:6. Alternate translation: [he does not worship the idols] or [he does not pray to the idols]

The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelite people group]

17.note: This word refers to the money paid by a person to use borrowed money. However, some modern versions interpret “interest” in this passage as “too much interest.”
Yahweh speaks of obeying his statutes as if his statutes were a path in which the person walks. Alternate translation: [obeys my statutes]

18.note:
# General Information:

Yahweh speaks about the son’s father who has not obeyed God’s law.
to take something from someone else by using threats or force.
Alternate translation: [pay attention, because what I am about to say is both true and important: he]

19.q: Why does the son not bear the iniquity of his father?
19.note: Yahweh speaks of a person being responsible for or guilty of iniquity as if the iniquity were an object that the person carries. Alternate translation: [Why is the son not responsible for the iniquity of his father?] or [Why is the son not guilty of the iniquity of his father?]

20.q: The righteousness of the one who acts rightly will be on himself
20.note: For righteousness to be on a person is an idiom that means the person is responsible for that righteousness. Alternate translation: [The one who acts rightly will be responsible for his own righteousness]

20.q: the wickedness of the wicked will be on himself
20.note: For wickedness to be on a person is an idiom that means the person is responsible for that wickedness. Alternate translation: [the wicked person will be responsible for his own wickedness]

21.note:
# General Information:

Yahweh speaking of the wicked person who changes and does what is righteous.

22.q: All the transgressions that he has committed will not be called to mind against him
22.note: The idiom “call to mind” means to remember. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I will not remember all the transgressions that he has committed and will not hold them against him] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

22.q: by the righteousness that he practices
22.note: Alternate translation: [because of the righteous things he has done]

23.note:
# General Information:

Yahweh speaks about his desire for wicked people.

23.q: Do I greatly rejoice over the death of the wicked … and not in his turning away from his way so that he may live?
23.note: Yahweh asks this rhetorical question in order to emphasize the opposite. Alternate translation: [I do not greatly rejoice over the death of the wicked … but I do greatly rejoice if he turns away from his way so that he may live.]

23.q: this is the Lord Yahweh’s declaration
23.note: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 5:11. Alternate translation: [this is what the Lord Yahweh has declared] or [this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, have declared]

23.q: not in his turning away from his way
23.note: Yahweh speaks of a person’s lifestyle or behavior as if it were a way on which the person walks. The idiom “to turn away” from something means to stop doing that thing. Alternate translation: [not in his ceasing to live the way that he lives] (See also: [Idiom](ta:figs-idiom))

24.note:
# General Information:

Yahweh gives an example of a man who turns from righteousness to wickedness.
Yahweh asks this rhetorical question to emphasize the negative answer. Alternate translation: [then he will surely not live.]

24.q: All the righteousness that he had done will not be called to mind
24.note: The idiom “call to mind” means to remember. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I will not remember all the righteousness that he had done] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))
crime done against a country or against God, by someone who is expected to be loyal

24.q: he will die in the sins
24.note: Alternate translation: [he will die because of the sins]

25.note: The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelite people group]
Yahweh asks this rhetorical question to emphasize the negative answer. Alternate translation: [My ways are not unfair.]

25.q: Is it not your ways that are unfair?
25.note: Yahweh asks this rhetorical question to emphasize the positive answer. Alternate translation: [It is your ways that are unfair.]

26.q: dies because of them … die in the iniquity that he has done
26.note: These phrases repeat the thought of a man dying because of his sin to express that it was his fault and the fault of no one else.

28.note: Yahweh speaks of the person thinking about and understanding something as if the person were seeing it. Alternate translation: [he has considered] or [he has understood]

29.note: The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelite people group]

29.q: The way of the Lord is not fair … How is my way not fair … It is your ways that are not fair
29.note: Actions or behaviors are spoken of as if they were a way or path that a person travels. Alternate translation: [The Lord does not act fairly … How do I not act fairly … It is you who do not act fairly]

30.note: Yahweh speaks of a person’s actions as if the person were walking along a path. Alternate translation: [according to his actions]

30.q: turn away from all your transgressions so that they will not be stumbling blocks of iniquity against you
30.note: Yahweh speaks of “transgressions” causing people to rebel against him as if they were blocks over which the people stumble.

30.q: stumbling blocks of iniquity against you
30.note: This could mean: (1) the stumbling blocks cause the person to commit more iniquity. Alternate translation: [stumbling blocks that cause you to commit more iniquity] or (2) The word [iniquity] is a metonym for the punishment that a person receives for his iniquity. Alternate translation: [stumbling blocks that lead to your punishment]

31.q: Throw away from yourselves all of the transgressions that you have committed
31.note: Yahweh speaks of the people determining to stop committing transgressions as if the transgressions were objects, such as clothing, that they removed and threw away. Alternate translation: [Get rid of all of the transgressions that you have committed]

31.q: make for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit
31.note: Here the word “heart” represents the will and emotions and the word “spirit” represents the thoughts and disposition. Yahweh speaks of the people having new emotions and thoughts as if they were making a new heart and spirit for themselves. Alternate translation: [get for yourselves new emotions and a new way of thinking] (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

31.q: Why should you die, house of Israel?
31.note: Yahweh asks this rhetorical question to comfort the people of Israel. Alternate translation: [There is no reason for you to die, house of Israel.]

The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelite people group]
